summary: This paper investigates the large Davenport constant D(H_p^3) of the Heisenberg group of order p^3 and exponent p for odd primes. It proves the general bounds 3p - 1 <= D(H_p^3) <= 4p - 4, which strictly separates D(H_p^3) from its Loewy length 4p - 3 (in sharp contrast to M_27). It also establishes new lower bounds for the short-subsequence invariants eta and s. The methodology combines symplectic exponential coordinates, Cauchy-Davenport contraction, heavy-line elimination, and property B structure-theorem cross-splitting. All results are corroborated by a zero-import Lean 4 formalization and exact computational verifications.
strengths: Completely eliminates the previous upper bound 5p - 4 down to 4p - 4 using novel heavy-line elimination and structure-theorem cross-splitting.
Provides two explicit, non-isomorphic extremal minimal product-one sequences of length 3p - 1 witnessing the lower bound.
Fully mechanized zero-import Lean 4 formalization alongside rigorous computational verification across small primes.
weaknesses: The analysis involves intricate combinatorial case distinctions, particularly in eliminating residual structural obstructions (O1) and (O2) for p >= 5.
Exact tightness at 3p - 1 remains open as Conjecture 6.1 for p >= 5, leaving a small remaining structural gap.
strong_novelty_candidates: The symplectic exponential coordinate framework reducing word products to affine functionals of ordered areas in F_p^2.
Heavy-line elimination and structure-theorem cross-splitting lemmas for zero-sum sequences in nilpotent p-groups.
Zero-import Lean 4 verification of non-abelian zero-sum invariants.
